title: The Calling of St Matthew
museum: Contarelli Chapel, San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome
videoFormat: Step inside the painting: 9:16 seamless flythrough loop
caption:
Who's he pointing at? 👉

Christ walks into a Roman tax office and points. For 400 years everyone agreed the bearded man was Matthew, pointing at himself: "Me?" Then, in the 1980s, a few scholars said no. He's pointing at the boy counting coins, the one who won't look up.

Swipe for the hands that borrow from Michelangelo, a beam of light that matches the chapel's real window, and the apostle the X-rays say wasn't there at first. Plus the painter who became famous overnight, then killed a man.

Save this for your next trip to Rome, and watch the reel to step inside the painting.

notes: Matthew identity hedged: majority view = bearded man (Lavin, Röttgen); minority = young man at the end of the table (Prater 1985, Hass 1988; revived by Sara Magister 2012). X-ray claim (Christ's arm first higher, Peter added later) comes from Italian secondary sources (Avvenire 2012, Artribune, citing radiographs). We did not see the original technical report. Window alignment is phrased as 'the only window sits on that same side' (the chapel's single natural light source is to the right of the Calling on the left wall). Plate uses the Commons full-width image; the crops come from our 9770px scan (slightly cropped at the edges). Pope Francis quote ('This is me, a sinner on whom the Lord has turned his gaze') is available for a caption variant (America Magazine 2013 interview).
